title: What is the Chandrayaan-3 mission's key scientific result?

sources.title: Chandrayaan-3 - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Chandrayaan-3 (CHUN-drə-YAHN / ˌtʃʌndrəˈjɑːn /) is the third mission in the Chandrayaan programme, a series of lunar-exploration missions developed by ISRO. The mission consists of Vikram, a lunar lander, and Pragyan, a lunar rover, as replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which had crashed on landing in 2019.

sources.snippet: Mar 1, 2024 · It is equipped with a Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. An in-depth review is carried out to discuss the findings of the Chandrayaan-3 mission. The goals of Chandrayaan-3's mission are: (a) to show a safe and soft landing on the surface of the Moon; (b) to showcase roving lunar rover technology; and (c) to carry out in-situ scientific research.

answer: The sources do not single out one "key" scientific result, but they list several notable findings from the mission [4]. The clearest headline result is that the LIBS instrument on the rover confirmed the presence of sulphur on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [4]. Other results include the APXS instrument detecting minor elements, the ChaSTE payload making temperature observations, the ILSA instrument recording movements around the landing site, and RAMBHA-LP measuring near-surface plasma content [4]. Scientists also estimated that about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith were ejected and displaced over an area of 108.4 m² around the landing site [4]. The mission itself was designed to demonstrate safe landing, rover roving, and in-situ scientific experiments, rather than aiming for a single specific scientific discovery [3][6].
